workouts.warmup: 5 min bike or row, band pull-aparts x20, arm circles, shoulder CARs, push-up x10 slow

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Retract scapulae hard before unracking. Lower to lower chest with control. Drive through the full foot. Own the negative.
30-45° bench. Feel the upper chest stretch at the bottom. Squeeze hard at the top. Don't let the elbows flare beyond 45°.
Initiate with scapular depression. Pull elbows to ribs. Full stretch at top — don't short-change the ROM.
Chest on pad removes lower back. Pure upper back pull. Retract and depress scaps at the top of each rep.
This is a stretch exercise. Own the bottom. Slight elbow bend throughout. Don't let the stretch become reckless.
Rope to face height. Elbows high and wide. External rotate hard at the end. Shoulder health non-negotiable.

workouts.finisher: Cable Chest Press: 3 sets of 20 reps with minimal rest (30s) — pump and blood flow focus
workouts.cooldown: Doorway chest stretch 60s each side, lat hang 45s, child's pose 60s, thoracic extension on foam roller 90s
workouts.progressionNotes: Add 2.5kg to bench when all 4 sets hit 10 reps with clean form. Add 1 rep per session on accessories before increasing weight.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike, leg swings x10 each, hip circles, goblet squat x10 bodyweight, glute bridge x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Brace 360° before descent. Break hips and knees simultaneously. Drive knees out. Think about pushing the floor away, not just standing up.
Hip hinge — push hips back, not down. Maintain neutral spine. Feel the hamstring stretch load. Drive hips through at the top.
Feet low on platform for quad emphasis. Don't lock out at top. Control the negative — this is where growth happens.
Rear foot on bench. Stay tall. Sink the back knee toward the floor. Drive through front heel. This will be uncomfortable. That's the point.
High-rep pump set. Don't lock out knees. Control the descent. Press through the full foot evenly.
Slow eccentric is the gold. Lower as far as you can control. Use hands to push back up if needed. Hamstring length-tension at its best.

workouts.finisher: Wall Sit: 3 x max hold (aim 45-60s) with 30s rest — quad burnout
workouts.cooldown: Seated hamstring stretch 60s each, pigeon pose 90s each, quad stretch 45s each, hip flexor lunge 60s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Prioritise squat strength. Add 2.5-5kg when all sets hit top of rep range. Track weekly volume (sets x reps x load) and aim for 5-10% increase monthly.

workouts.warmup: Band pull-aparts x25, wall slides x10, shoulder CARs x5 each, incline push-up x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Lead with upper chest. Full stretch at bottom. Squeeze hard at top. This is your strength prime mover today — don't go too light.
Seated or standing. Full ROM — all the way up, all the way down. Control the eccentric. Neutral or pronated grip depending on shoulder comfort.
Constant cable tension beats barbell for chest isolation. Squeeze pecs at lockout. Don't let the weight drift. Chest-to-cable connection is the goal.
Lead with elbows, not wrists. Slight forward lean. Don't shrug. Control the descent — it builds the muscle, not the lift up.
Lean forward for pec emphasis. Go to full depth. If this is easy, add weight next session. If hard, reduce reps — don't shorten ROM.
Lower to forehead or behind head. Elbows stay stationary. Full extension at top. Tricep long head emphasis — critical for arm size.

workouts.finisher: Diamond Push-Up: AMRAP x2 with 30s rest — tricep and inner pec burnout
workouts.cooldown: Cross-body shoulder stretch 45s each, overhead tricep stretch 45s each, doorway chest stretch 60s each side
workouts.progressionNotes: Rotate primary lift weekly between Barbell Bench and Incline DB Press. Lateral raises: add 1 rep per week before increasing weight.

workouts.workoutName: Pull Day — Back & Bicep Width Builder
workouts.warmup: Dead hangs 3x20s, scapular pull-ups x10, band pull-aparts x20, face pull x15 light

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Full dead hang start. Depress and retract scaps before pulling. Chin over bar. Don't kip. Add load when all reps are clean.
Hinge to 45° and hold. Row to lower abdomen. Elbows drive back, not out. Squeeze the back at the top. Control the bar down.
Wide grip. Pull to upper chest. Let the lat fully stretch at the top. Think of driving elbows to your hip pockets.
Rotate into the row for full lat stretch at the bottom. Anti-rotation demand on the core. Own the contraction at the end of each rep.
Hinge 45°+. Arc arms out to side. Slight elbow bend. Don't shrug. Rear delts are chronically underdeveloped — prioritise them.
Don't swing. Slow eccentric is the growth driver. Supinate at the top. Full ROM from extended arm to peak contraction.

workouts.finisher: Chin-Up: max reps x2 sets / Lat Pulldown: 2 x 20 (if pull-ups are limited) — 60s rest
workouts.cooldown: Lat stretch on rack 45s each side, bicep wall stretch 45s each, thoracic foam roll 90s, child's pose 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Track total weighted pull-up volume. Progress weighted pull-up before adding more accessory volume. Pull-ups are the king of back development.

workouts.warmup: 10 min walk/light bike, hip hinge drills with PVC, glute bridge x20, good morning x10 bodyweight

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Load the hamstrings eccentrically. Push hips back — don't round the lower back. Bar stays close to legs. Full hip extension at top.
Upper back on bench. Bar over hip crease. Drive hips to full extension. 2-second hold at top. Posterior pelvic tilt at top. Glutes, not lower back.
Most potent hamstring exercise on the planet. Slow eccentric is the goal. Use hands at the bottom if needed. Build up gradually.
Elbows inside knees at bottom. Upright torso. Full depth. This is a quad accessory today — go deep and feel the quad stretch.
Hip hinge on one leg. Control the balance — don't sacrifice it for load. Hamstring stretch is the goal. Dumbbell in opposite hand for balance.
Full ROM every rep. Pause and stretch at the bottom. Soleus emphasis (knee bent). Calves are trained through stretch — short reps are wasted reps.

workouts.finisher: Glute Bridge Pulse: 3 x 30 reps bodyweight — glute endurance and blood flow
workouts.cooldown: Seated hamstring stretch 90s each, figure-four glute stretch 60s each, calf wall stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Track RDL load weekly. Add 5kg when all 4 sets complete at top of rep range. Hip thrust: add 5-10kg when 15 reps feel controlled.

workouts.warmup: 5 min row, cat-cow x10, glute bridge x15, incline push-up x10, band pull-apart x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Hold weight at chest. Elbows inside knees at bottom. Upright torso is the goal here. Build the squat pattern before loading it heavily.
Greater ROM than barbell. Control the stretch. Squeeze at the top. Elbows 45° from body — not flaring wide.
Brace on bench. Drive elbow back — think elbow to ceiling. Squeeze the lat at the top. Don't let the shoulder drop.
Hinge pattern priority. Push hips back. Maintain flat back throughout. Bar or dumbbells stay close. Feel the hamstring load.
Full ROM. Control it down. Seat back support is fine for beginners. Don't overarch the lower back to press more.
Ribs down. Glutes squeezed. Breathe rhythmically. No sagging hips. Quality over duration — don't just survive the timer.

workouts.finisher: Bodyweight Squat x20 + Push-Up x10: 3 rounds with 45s rest — total body pump
workouts.cooldown: Hip flexor lunge stretch 60s each, chest doorway stretch 45s each, lat stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Beginner-focused. Log every session. Increase weight by smallest increment when top rep range is achieved with full control. Never sacrifice form for load.

workouts.warmup: Arm circles, band pull-aparts x20, light DB curl x15, push-down x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Hands shoulder-width or slightly closer. Elbows tuck close to ribs. Tricep emphasis. Lower to lower chest. Biggest tricep builder in the gym.
No swinging. Slow eccentric is non-negotiable. Full ROM. Supinate and squeeze hard at the top. Elbows stay at sides.
Lower to forehead or behind. Elbows stationary. Full extension. Tricep long head = biggest portion of the arm. Train it hard.
Bench at 45°. Arms hang back — maximum stretch on the long head. Curl without swinging body. Massive growth stimulus.
Stay upright for tricep emphasis. Full ROM down. Lockout at top. Add weight if bodyweight is too easy.
Neutral grip. Works brachialis and brachioradialis. Key for arm thickness and forearm development. Control both ways.

workouts.finisher: Curl-to-Press: 3 x 10 — bicep curl straight into overhead press — integrated pump
workouts.cooldown: Overhead tricep stretch 45s each, bicep wall stretch 45s each, wrist flexor/extensor stretch 30s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Arms respond to volume. Track total sets per week (aim for 12-16 sets per muscle). Increase weight when top of rep range is clean for all sets.

workouts.warmup: Band pull-aparts x30, wall slides x10, shoulder CARs, push-up x15, light bench x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Heavy strength focus. Maximise mechanical tension. Full arch, leg drive, tight upper back. The foundation of chest mass.
Upper chest is often underdeveloped. Control the stretch. Elbows slightly tucked. Squeeze at top. This is your hypertrophy block.
Lean forward for pec. Full ROM every rep. If 15 reps is easy, add a plate. Lower chest needs direct volume.
Cables from low position, arc up and together. Upper chest and anterior delt. Constant tension — peak contraction focus.
Long head overloaded here. Behind the head maximises stretch. Elbows absolutely stationary. This is a precision exercise.
End of session burnout. Full ROM. Don't compensate with faster reps. Quality reps only. Stop before form breaks.

workouts.finisher: Cable Chest Press: 3 x 25 with 30s rest — high-rep pump to maximise hypertrophic stimulus
workouts.cooldown: Doorway chest stretch 90s each side, overhead tricep stretch 60s each, PVC thoracic extension 90s
workouts.progressionNotes: Advanced: use double progression — increase reps first, then weight. Periodise bench: 4 weeks ascending load, 1 week deload.

workouts.warmup: Dead hangs 3x20s, scapular pull-ups x10, band rows x15, light barbell row x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Heaviest compound row. Hinge to 45°. Pull to belly button. Upper back contracted hard. This builds thickness — rows beat pull-ups for back size.
Width comes from pull-ups. Slow eccentric is the stimulus. Full hang at bottom. Chest to bar target. Don't kip.
Close neutral grip. Chest on pad. Drive elbows back. Full range of motion. Rhomboids and mid-traps are the target.
Landmine row variation. Pull in an arc. High elbow at top. Teres major and lats get a unique stretch at the bottom. Underrated exercise.
Rear delt health. Elbows high and wide. External rotate hard. Do this every session — shoulder longevity depends on it.
Heavy curl. No swing. 3-second negative. Supinate at top. Bicep peak development requires full ROM and a strong eccentric.

workouts.finisher: Chin-Up mechanical dropset: max reps with load → strip weight → max bodyweight reps — 2 rounds
workouts.cooldown: Lat stretch on rack 60s each side, bicep stretch on wall 45s each, thoracic extension foam roll 2 min
workouts.progressionNotes: Advanced back training requires managing cumulative fatigue. Rotate primary row (Barbell vs T-Bar) every 4 weeks. Monitor shoulder health closely.

workouts.warmup: Glute bridge x20, clamshell x15 each, hip circle x10 each, resistance band walk x20m each direction

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: The premier glute builder. Bar on pad over hips. Drive to full extension. 2-second squeeze at top. Posterior pelvic tilt matters — don't hyperextend the lumbar.
Hamstring stretch-focused. Push hips back further than you think. Maintain flat back. Drive hips through at top. Glutes fire hard in the top half.
Front foot further from bench for more glute. Sink deep. Drive through heel. Glutes and hamstrings at long length = maximal stimulus.
Wide stance, toes 45°. Knees track toes. Inner thigh and glute emphasis. Go deep. Squeeze glutes hard at the top.
The eccentric hamstring king. Lower as slowly as possible. Catch yourself at the bottom. Build over weeks — this is a serious exercise.
Balance challenge + hamstring work. Don't sacrifice depth for balance. Hold dumbbell in opposite hand. Hip stability is the bonus adaptation.

workouts.finisher: Hip Thrust Burnout: 3 x 20 bodyweight, 30s rest — glute endurance finish
workouts.cooldown: Pigeon pose 90s each, figure-four 60s each, lying hamstring stretch 60s each, hip flexor lunge 60s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Hip thrust progression: target 1-1.5x bodyweight for 10 reps within 12 weeks. Track unilateral imbalances and correct before adding load.

workouts.warmup: Band pull-aparts x25, face pulls x15 light, arm circles, shoulder CARs x5 each direction

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Full ROM is non-negotiable. Don't quarter-rep. Seated for stability. Control the eccentric. This is your strength anchor today.
Width comes from lateral delts. Lead with elbows. Don't shrug. Slow descent builds the muscle. 5 sets is appropriate — laterals are hard to overload.
Rope at face height. Elbows high. External rotate hard at the end. Rear delts and rotator cuff health. Never skip these.
Hinge 45°+. Lift arms to side. Rear delts — the most neglected part of the shoulder. Consistent high volume here changes your physique.
Start with palms facing you, rotate to face out as you press. Hits all three delt heads through the rotation. Controlled throughout.
Elbows lead and stay slightly above wrists. Pull to mid-chest. Don't go too wide — keep wrists below elbow level for shoulder safety.

workouts.finisher: Lateral Raise dropset: heavy x10 → medium x10 → light x10 — 3 rounds, 60s rest. Lateral delt obliteration.
workouts.cooldown: Cross-body shoulder stretch 60s each, neck side stretch 45s each, doorway stretch 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Lateral raises: prioritise feel over weight. Better to do 20 quality reps at 8kg than sloppy reps at 14kg. Film yourself occasionally to check form.

workouts.workoutName: Compound Strength — Full Body Heavy Day
workouts.warmup: 10 min general movement, hip hinge drills, band pull-aparts x20, empty bar warm-up sets x2

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Strength block. Heavy mechanical tension builds the most muscle. Bracing is critical. Drive your back into the bar on the way up.
Upper body press anchor. Leg drive. Tight arch. Bar path is an arc — not straight up. Touch and press — no bouncing.
Heavy row to match heavy press. Back thickness is built here. Pull to belly. Control the descent. The eccentric matters.
Posterior chain accessory. Heavy but controlled. Hamstring load is the stimulus. Don't bounce at the bottom.
Overhead strength after the primary movers. Full ROM. Don't rush. Shoulder stability earned through prior exercises supports this.
Back width cap to the session. Dead hang. Full ROM. If fatigued from rows, use a lighter band to maintain quality. Volume > load at this point.

workouts.finisher: Farmer's Carry: 4 x 30m with heavy dumbbells — grip, core, and total body finisher
workouts.cooldown: Full body stretch sequence — hip flexors, hamstrings, chest, lats, shoulders — 2 min total
workouts.progressionNotes: Heavy compound days require recovery. Sleep 8h minimum. Eat above maintenance. Log your lifts. Aim for 1-2% load increase per week on main lifts.

workouts.warmup: Jumping jacks x30, arm circles, hip hinge bodyweight x10, push-up x10, band pull-apart x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: On the floor if no bench. Full ROM limited, but control the negative. At home, technique discipline is your competitive advantage.
Brace on knee or chair. Elbow to ceiling. Control the descent. At home, this is your primary back builder — don't rush it.
Heavy goblet squat builds serious quad and glute muscle. Go deep. Elbows inside knees at bottom. Upright torso.
Dumbbell RDL. Hip hinge is the pattern. Load the hamstrings. Drive hips through. If dumbbells are too light, add reps or slow the tempo.
Standing or seated. Full ROM. If weight is limiting, increase reps to 20 and maintain slow tempo for time under tension.
Use a chair at an angle if no bench. Arms hang back. Full stretch. Slow eccentric. Best bicep exercise for home training.

workouts.finisher: Dumbbell Complex: Romanian Deadlift x8 + Bent-Over Row x8 + Shoulder Press x8 = 1 round. 3 rounds, 90s rest.
workouts.cooldown: Doorway chest stretch 60s, lat side stretch 45s each, hamstring seated stretch 60s each
workouts.progressionNotes: With limited equipment, progression comes through tempo, rep range, and exercise variation. Track total reps per session and aim to beat it weekly.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike, dynamic stretching, tempo push-up x5 (very slow), goblet squat x8 slow

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: 5-second descent. 1-second pause. This is painful and productive. Muscles are maximally loaded through the full range. Lighter weight than normal — that's correct.
4-second descent. Full stretch. Don't touch shoulders. Squeeze hard at the top. Time under tension method maximises hypertrophy at lower loads.
3-second controlled return to full stretch. Lat under load for longer. This is a different stimulus to normal tempo — embrace it.
4-second hip hinge down. Hamstrings loaded slowly and deeply. 1-second pause at the stretch. Drive hips through assertively at the top.
Stretch-focused exercise already — add 4-second descent and it becomes elite. Chest muscle growth is all about time in the lengthened position.
6-second eccentric. The slowest thing you'll do in the gym. Hamstring lengthened-state loading is the most potent hypertrophy signal for posterior chain.

workouts.finisher: Pause Squat: 3 x 10 with 2-second pause at bottom — sustained quad tension
workouts.cooldown: Full body stretch — extra time on each position given the deep muscle fatigue from tempo work. Minimum 10 min.
workouts.progressionNotes: Tempo training: reduce load 20-30% compared to normal. Progression = maintain tempo perfectly, then add small load. Muscles don't count reps — they feel time.

workouts.workoutName: Upper Body Volume Day — High Rep Hypertrophy
workouts.warmup: Arm circles, band pull-aparts x20, push-up x15, lat pulldown x15 light, shoulder press x10 light

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Machine isolates the chest beautifully for high-rep work. Control both ways. Squeeze at lockout. Higher rep ranges increase metabolic stress.
High rep pulldown. Full stretch at top. Drive elbows down. Blood flow to the lats is the goal today — pump-focused training works.
High-rep laterals build width. Light weight. Perfect form. Lead with elbows. Control down. 5 sets x 20-25 reps = serious delt volume.
Constant tension from cables. Squeeze hard at lockout. Don't let the weight pull you into a bad position. Pure pump work.
Rear delt health and volume. High rep, light weight. External rotation at the end. These reps are cumulative — do them every push session.
Neutral grip. Brachialis and forearm pump. No swing. Control down. Combined with other volume, this finishes the arms completely.

workouts.finisher: Push-Up x25 + Band Pull-Apart x25: 3 rounds, 45s rest — chest/rear delt superset pump finisher
workouts.cooldown: Doorway chest stretch 60s each side, lat stretch 45s each, neck and shoulder mobility 2 min
workouts.progressionNotes: Volume-focused day. Track total reps per exercise. Goal is progressive overload through volume, not load. Add 1-2 reps per set each week before increasing weight.

workouts.warmup: Hip circle x10 each, single leg balance drills, lateral step-up x10 each, single arm press x10 each light

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: The king of unilateral leg training. Sink deep. Front foot controls emphasis — forward for glutes, more upright for quads. Address imbalances here.
Single arm requires core anti-rotation. Heavier relative stimulus than bilateral. Don't let the torso rotate. Pec isolation is enhanced.
Rotate into the row for full lat stretch. Unilateral rows allow greater range of motion than barbell variations. Own the stretch.
Unilateral hinge. Balance is secondary to the hip hinge. Slow and controlled. Great for hamstring and glute independence.
Shift weight to one arm per rep. The working arm carries significantly more load. Progression toward one-arm push-up. Core demand is high.
Drive through the top foot. Don't push off the bottom. Full hip extension at the top. Quad and glute unilateral volume.

workouts.finisher: Deficit Reverse Lunge: 3 x 10 each leg with bodyweight — deep quad and glute stretch to finish
workouts.cooldown: Pigeon pose 90s each, single leg hamstring stretch 60s each, cross-body shoulder stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Unilateral training identifies and corrects side-to-side imbalances. Lead with the weaker side. Match the stronger side's reps/load — don't exceed it.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike at moderate pace, leg swings x10, bodyweight squat x15, leg extension light x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Most quad-dominant squat variation. Elbows high is non-negotiable. Deep knee flexion. Upright torso removes posterior chain and loads the quads maximally.
Feet low on platform. Don't lock out. Control the negative. Hack squat on machine gives safe overload of the quads without lower back fatigue.
High feet placement shifts to glutes. Low feet = quads. Today = low feet, moderate width. Control the descent — don't let the sled drop.
4-second descent for quad time-under-tension. Lighter than normal is expected and appropriate. Muscle burn = stimulus.
High-rep pump set. Keep the weight moderate. This is about flushing blood through the quads and maintaining the stimulus at end of session.
Full stretch at the bottom — pause there. Rise to full contraction. Calves need range more than load. Gastrocnemius focus (knee straight).

workouts.finisher: Wall Sit: 3 x 45-60s — terminal quad isometric burnout
workouts.cooldown: Quad stretch 60s each, hip flexor lunge 60s each, calf stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Front squat mobility takes time. Don't sacrifice elbow height for load. Progress goblet squat first, then transition to front squat when positioning is solid.

workouts.workoutName: Full Body Muscle — Home Bodyweight Advanced
workouts.warmup: Jumping jacks x50, push-up x15, bodyweight squat x20, hip hinge x10, hollow body hold 20s

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Full ROM single leg squat. Control descent. Arms forward for balance. The most demanding bodyweight leg exercise. Strength and mobility combined.
Near-unilateral push. Maximum chest and tricep loading possible without weights. Earn this movement — wide push-up first if not ready.
Full ROM. Dead hang. 3-second negative. The best bodyweight back exercise. Volume here = back development.
Bodyweight or with any load available. Deep sink. Rear foot elevated. Quad and glute emphasis depending on torso lean.
Tricep isolation bodyweight style. Elbows track close. Full ROM. Use as accessory after archer push-ups — arms are pre-fatigued.
Supinated grip. More bicep. Full stretch at bottom. Chest to bar target. Slow negative for maximum bicep growth.

workouts.finisher: Burpee x5 + Push-Up x10 + Squat x15: 3 rounds, 60s rest — full body metabolic close
workouts.cooldown: Pigeon pose 90s each, lat stretch hanging 45s, doorway chest stretch 60s each, child's pose 90s
workouts.progressionNotes: Advanced bodyweight: progression is through weighted vest, tempo manipulation, or harder variations. Pistol squat strength is a long-term investment.

workouts.warmup: 5 min walk or bike, cat-cow x10, glute bridge x15, push-up x8, band row x12

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Learn the squat pattern here. Elbows inside knees. Chest tall. Upright. This is your foundation — everything else builds on it.
Safer than barbell for beginners. Control the weight. Feel the chest doing the work. Elbows 45° from body.
Machine makes the pattern accessible. Pull elbows to ribs. Full stretch at top. You're building the pull-up here — every rep matters.
Hip hinge is a fundamental human movement. Push hips back. Neutral spine. Feel the hamstring load. Light weight first — this is a skill.
Seated for stability. Full ROM. Don't overarch the lower back. Shoulders work independently of each other — note any asymmetry.
Core stability. Ribs down. Glutes on. Breathe. Build toward 60s over 4-6 weeks. Quality beats duration every time.

workouts.finisher: Bodyweight Squat x15 + Push-Up x8: 2 rounds, 60s rest — reinforce patterns at session close
workouts.cooldown: Hip flexor lunge 60s each, hamstring seated stretch 45s each, chest stretch 45s, child's pose 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Beginners: increase weight by the smallest increment available when all sets and reps are completed with full control. Prioritise movement quality over load always.

workouts.workoutName: Mechanical Advantage Drop Set — Upper Body
workouts.warmup: Band pull-aparts x25, arm circles, shoulder CARs, light cable press x15, lat pulldown x15

mainWorkout.exercise: Incline Dumbbell Press → Flat DB Press → Decline Push-Up
mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Mechanical dropset: start in weakest position (incline), progress to stronger positions without rest. Maximises total chest volume and metabolic stress.

mainWorkout.exercise: Wide Grip Lat Pulldown → Neutral Grip Pulldown → Underhand Pulldown
mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Mechanical lat dropset — same cable, different grips in sequence. Each grip hits the back slightly differently. Massive lat volume in short time.
After the dropset, standard bench press to build raw strength on a pre-fatigued muscle. Lighter weight than normal. Chest connection should be excellent.
After pulldown dropset, pull-ups finish the lat work. Slow eccentric. Full ROM. If fatigued, use band assistance to maintain quality.
Rear delt always. Every push/pull session. High rep, controlled, consistent. Never skip these.
Rotator cuff and rear delt health. External rotate hard. Elbows high. Shoulder longevity over decades starts with consistent face pulls.

workouts.finisher: Push-Up x20 + Chin-Up x8: 3 superset rounds, 60s rest — bilateral upper body burnout
workouts.cooldown: Doorway stretch 60s each side, lat bar hang 45s, cross-body stretch 45s each, thoracic foam roll 2 min
workouts.progressionNotes: Mechanical dropsets are an advanced technique — use sparingly (once per 2 weeks per muscle group). Standard sets the rest of the time for progressive overload.
